text.p: Oil prices tumbled on Friday as traders bet that forecasts for milder weather in the Northeast of America would curtail demand for heating oil.
Base metals prices were firmer but gold, silver and wheat prices were lower, pushing the CRB index of 17 commodities 1.58 points down to 238.99.
A late flurry of buying during Friday afternoon LME trading kept most base metals on the boil, with prices largely firmer at the close.
New York precious metals futures end lower for the fourth straight day Friday, with gold and platinum sliding to new three year lows, though volumes were not as heavy as Thursday.
"Sentiment in precious metals is extremely poor, though volumes were not that heavy today," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
"Both the funds and bullion banks were selling today, with talk of European central bank sales still around," he said.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.50 an ounce at $346.00, after posting a new contract low at $345.40.
Estimated total gold futures volume was 40,000 lots, down from Thursday's official volume of 79,505 contracts.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $344.10/60, after fixing at a $345.50 in London Friday afternoon, just up from a new three and a quarter year low at $345.00 at the London morning fix. Spot gold closed in New York Thursday quoted $345.35/85.

COMEX March silver, which jumped near the close Thursday, fell back to a low $4.810 intraday Friday, before ending down 3.5 cents at $4.970. NYMEX April platinum closed down $2.90 at $353.00 an ounce, after seeing a new contract low at $351.00.

Huge fund selling and bearish export talk hammered CBOT wheat futures to a sharply lower close with nearby March and May ratcheting to new contract lows amid fast trading in late dealings, traders said. Wheat closed two to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 10-1/2 at $3.59-3/4.

Fund selling was estimated from 20 million to 30 million bushels. The contract low for March is $3.57 a bushel, down from the previous low of $3.63 set November 6. The new low for May is $3.47, down from the previous low of $3.48. Fundamentals also
remained suspect with India and Egypt central to the bearish export talk.

Oil prices tumbled Friday as traders bet forecasts for milder weather in the Northeast would curtail demand for heating oil. Weather Services Corp. forecast that temperatures in the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, would moderate to normal to slightly above normal next week.

March crude oil fell 72 cents to $24.15 a barrel. Heating oil for February delivery lost 1.69 cents to 68.65 cents a gallon and February gasoline fell 1.35 cents to 68.47 cents a gallon at the New York Mercantile Exchange. Friday was also the final trading day for the February contracts, which prompted volatile trading in the session.
